body.statement: If \(b\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(p:[0,\eta)\to\mathcal P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is a one-sided differentiable legal path with \(p(0)=b\), then \(\dot p(0+)\in\mathcal D_b\). For every \(g\in\mathcal D_b\) that is generated by such a legal path, \(d_b(g)\) equals the genuine one-sided derivative \(\partial_+\Phi\{p(t)\}|_{t=0}\). Thus values of \(d_b\) outside \(\mathcal D_b\) provide a total calibration convention but no ambient-to-legal realization theorem.
body.justification: The domain lemma separates derivatives of legal observed-law paths from algebraic directions introduced solely to make calibration total.
body.gap: Generic directional calculus does not identify which zero-cell scores arise from the binary-instrument causal-law image.
body.consumer: The legal realization argument can target exactly the admissible tangent scores without claiming an invalid ambient lift.
